ai.definition: Mechanistic interpretability is a research approach that aims to understand the internal mechanisms of neural networks by reverse-engineering their internal circuits. This method contrasts with traditional black-box approaches where the inner workings of models are not transparent.
ai.howItWorks: Researchers use techniques such as sparse autoencoders and causal interventions to isolate features and circuits within model activations, mapping out how specific behaviors arise from these internal processes.
ai.problemSolved: Addressing the lack of transparency in AI systems, particularly neural networks, by providing a clearer understanding of how models arrive at their decisions and behaviors.
ai.manufacturing: Not directly involved as it is primarily a research methodology rather than a product or service.
ai.buildProcess: Involves developing algorithms for sparse autoencoders, implementing causal interventions, and analyzing model activations to identify key features and circuits responsible for specific behaviors.
ai.costDrivers: High computational resources required for data processing and analysis; expertise in machine learning and interpretability is also a significant cost driver.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Emerging from lab research, with potential to transition into early commercial applications as understanding of mechanisms improves.
ai.regulation: Currently not regulated due to its stage of development; however, future regulations may be required as it becomes more widely adopted in critical AI systems.
ai.risks: Risk of misinterpretation or oversimplification of complex models; potential for misuse if interpretability leads to overconfidence in model decisions.
ai.profitability: Not yet directly profitable but has the potential to improve AI safety and reliability, which could lead to increased trust and adoption of AI systems in critical applications.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development may involve integrating mechanistic interpretability with other explainable AI techniques to enhance overall transparency and accountability of AI models.

glossary.def: A type of neural network used for feature learning, where the hidden layer has fewer nodes than the input layer.
An experimental method in which a variable is manipulated to observe its effect on another variable, often used to understand cause-and-effect relationships within models.

subsystems.name: Behavioural testbeds
subsystems.role: create narrow, verifiable behaviours that can actually be explained.
parts: prompt datasets with one controlled variable
model organisms (deliberately backdoored or deceptive small models)

subsystems.name: Activation readout
subsystems.role: measure what information is linearly present at each layer and token position.

subsystems.name: Sparse feature extraction
subsystems.role: break dense activations into a larger set of sparsely active, human-readable directions.

subsystems.name: Causal intervention
subsystems.role: test whether a component actually causes the behaviour, not just correlates with it.

subsystems.name: Circuit assembly and verification
subsystems.role: join components and features into a graph that predicts behaviour.

subsystems.name: Safety application
subsystems.role: turn explanations into oversight of real models.

buildSteps.title: Choose a behaviour and an open model
buildSteps.detail: Pick something narrow and checkable — which token is predicted, or whether an answer is truthful — on a model whose weights and activations can be inspected.

buildSteps.title: Build a controlled dataset
buildSteps.detail: Write prompt pairs that differ in exactly one factor, so the effect of that factor on the output can be measured cleanly.

buildSteps.title: Sweep for where the behaviour lives
buildSteps.detail: Patch activations from one run into another, layer by layer and position by position, to find the places that change the answer.

buildSteps.title: Zoom into components
buildSteps.detail: Inspect the attention heads and MLP blocks flagged by the sweep, using logit lens and attribution to see what each writes to the residual stream.

buildSteps.title: Decompose into features
buildSteps.detail: Train sparse autoencoders on activations at the interesting layers, so a dense vector is replaced by a short list of active directions.

buildSteps.title: Label the features
buildSteps.detail: Find the inputs that fire each feature most strongly, describe it in words, and have a language model draft explanations for review.

buildSteps.title: Verify causally
buildSteps.detail: Clamp or steer each candidate feature up and down and check the behaviour moves as predicted — a feature must be both sufficient and necessary.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and test a circuit
buildSteps.detail: Connect the verified features and components into one explanation, then check it predicts answers on prompts never used during the analysis.

buildSteps.title: Stress-test and scale
buildSteps.detail: Repeat on other prompts, larger or retrained models, and realistic deception or backdoor settings to see whether the explanation survives.

prerequisites.tech: Open models with weight and activation access
prerequisites.why: the analysis needs the internal tensors, not just the text a model outputs.

prerequisites.tech: Large-scale compute for interventions and SAE training
prerequisites.why: training a sparse autoencoder on a frontier model's activations is a substantial training run in its own right.
sparse autoencoders recover interpretable features at frontier scale, but coverage is incomplete and reconstruction is imperfect.
toy models and deliberately misaligned model organisms let methods be checked against a known answer before use on unknown models.
there is no agreed test for whether a circuit explanation is complete or faithful rather than merely plausible.

pathway.milestone: reproducible circuits in small models and millions of extracted features in large ones
pathway.unlocks: a working vocabulary of features for describing model internals.

pathway.milestone: reliable automated labelling and shared benchmarks for interpretability
pathway.unlocks: methods that can be compared and scaled beyond a few well-studied models.

pathway.milestone: interpretability used as a live safety check during training and deployment
pathway.unlocks: a warning system that does not depend on catching bad behaviour in outputs.

pathway.milestone: near-complete explanations usable to audit a model before release
pathway.unlocks: safety claims about frontier systems that can be checked rather than asserted.
